quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells you to slow down and be ready to stop. You must let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: You miss your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Never stop, back up, or swerve across lanes on the highway. Never cross the median to turn around. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic go first. You only need to stop if other cars are coming.

questions.question: Do not pass in these situations:

options.text: On a hill or around a curve.
When a school bus has flashing lights.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on a hill, around a curve, at an intersection, near a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in a no passing zone. Do not pass a school bus with red flashing lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should take care of your physical health. This means you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular checkups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only when you feel well.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical health affects how safely you can drive. Know your physical limits and only drive when you feel well.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Copy what other drivers are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, always follow their directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle coming. You should:

options.text: Ignore it if other lanes are open.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move to give space, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give space, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, slow down, move your car out of the way, and stop. Never try to outrun an emergency vehicle.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks:

options.text: Need more distance to stop than cars do.
Pass faster going downhill than cars do.
Turn in a smaller space than cars do.
Pass faster going uphill than cars do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more distance to stop than cars do.
questions.explanation: Trucks are large and heavy. They need longer distances to stop than cars.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Let pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: Driving after drinking alcohol is:

options.text: A minor problem.
A serious safety problem.
Safe if you have only a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A serious safety problem.
questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely if you drink alcohol or take drugs. It is dangerous to you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: If you feel too tired to drive safely, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road and rest.
Drink a large energy drink.
Open all the windows and turn on the air conditioning.
Talk to a friend on the phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you cannot drive safely. Your reaction time and thinking get much worse. Take a rest break every two hours on long drives. If you get drowsy, pull off the road and rest.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to not drink alcohol and let time pass. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard lights to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard lights right away. Move as far off the road as you can. Raise your hood so other drivers know your car is broken down.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them from crossing against the light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light and they do not. Pedestrians come first.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are making a turn.
Your emergency brake is on.
You are changing lanes.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Your brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working properly at all times.

questions.question: If you have the right-of-way at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all other drivers will follow the right-of-way rules.
Wave other drivers to go first.
Drive through right away.
Look for cars, pedestrians, and bicycles before moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for cars, pedestrians, and bicycles before moving.
questions.explanation: Always look both ways before entering an intersection, even if you have the right-of-way. Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.question: When you signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb:

options.text: You only need to signal if other cars are near.
It is good driving practice and required by law.
You only need to signal while you are turning, not before.
You do not need to signal if you are moving slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is good driving practice and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal before you turn or change lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before you move left or right. Always signal before pulling away from the curb.

questions.question: Who must wear a fastened safety belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: The driver.
Front seat passengers.
Children ages 8 to 18.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: The driver and front seat passengers must wear safety belts. Children ages 8 to 18 must wear safety belts anywhere in the vehicle. This is the law.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Stay farther behind other cars.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. You should follow all these steps to stay safe on dark roads.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: Only for the driver.
For passengers on long drives.
For all passengers on highways.
For everyone every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: For everyone every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt at all times. In a crash, a person without a seat belt can become a flying object and hurt everyone in the car.

questions.question: What should you do about traffic signs and pavement markings?

options.text: Always obey them.
They are just suggestions.
Only follow them when there are other cars around.
Only follow them when a police officer is watching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always obey them.
questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic and keep drivers safe. You must always obey them.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Keep extra distance from that car.
Know that driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay focused on driving. Do not look at passengers, search for things, read, or daydream while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to crash.
